rows.description: Option A is chosen (pipeline_propose_change without run_id). Of the four decisions at the end of the plan only this one was answered; items 2-4 (.kodel/proposals/<name>.json git-ignored, the extra name argument for taking back, warnings left for a follow-up) stand as written unless said otherwise. The diff limit of the impl step was removed for this run, so the plan no longer has to fit 800 lines: drop the diff-limit estimate and the part of the Risks that talks about it.

Through pipeline_propose_change without run_id one must also be able to change an EXISTING pipeline, in this change and not as a follow-up. A name that is already in use is then a proposal to change that pipeline, not a refusal. Remove the follow-up 'Proposing a change of an existing pipeline outside a run' and the refusal on a name in use; a rename is not a change (a different name is a new pipeline).

pipeline_resolve without run_id returns only the parsed spec, not the YAML text, so an agent cannot start a change from the real file. Settle that resolve without run_id also returns the file's YAML and its hash, and that the tool description says to start from it.

rows.description: The proposal record must say whether it is new or a change, and for a change keep the hash of the file as it was when proposed. Accepting refuses if the file moved since (or the name appeared meanwhile for a new one), and for a change it replaces the existing file found by name or stem, not a new path. A no-op (nothing differs from the file) is refused like for a run.
For a change, show and the confirmation of apply must show what differs per step (the existing diffNodes) and the full YAML with the block of commands, not only the text.

Say what happens when a change of an existing pipeline is accepted while a run of it is going: runs keep their own copy, but the edit of the file is noticed by the existing mechanism for a hand-edited file and waits for the person; and the next pipeline_start asks working or committed version because the file is not committed. Cover both with a test.

SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS: the 'ask the person first' rule is for a run; a project-level proposal needs no asking, the person accepts anyway. pipeline_docs, topic pipeline-design, gets a short section on changing an existing pipeline (start from pipeline_resolve yaml, keep the name, change only what is needed). Add a real-agent scenario step or a second scenario for a change of an existing pipeline.
